full_judgment:
Sharif Uddin Chaklader J: This Rule at the instance of defendant No. 1-petitioner, directed against judgment and decree dated 13-5-2012 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Chandpur dismissing Title Appeal No. 141 of 2006 affirming those dated 12-1-2006 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Hajigonj, Chandpur decreeing Title Suit No. 23 of 2005.

2. It is the case of plaintiff that suit land originally belonged to Ana Gazi, whose name is recorded in CS khatian No. 37 and published finally, died, leaving sons, Abdul Kadir, who died, leaving 3 sons, Idris Miah, Kala Miah and Chand Miah. They became owner of the property of dag No. 548 by inheritance and in their names SA khatian No. 39 was prepared finally. The aforesaid heirs of Idris Gazi, defendant Nos. 2-5 by registered exchange deed No. 6707 dated 9-10-2003 exchanged 22 decimals of land with plaintiffs and delivered possession and in exchange defendant No. 2-5, got 29 decimals of land from plaintiffs. Defendant No. 1 on 3-6-2005 denied title of plaintiffs, hence the suit.

3. Defendant No. 1, in his written statement after taking preliminary objections as to maintainability of the suit, it is their case that while Jonab Ali Munshi was owner and possessor of the land of suit dag, by registered deed No. 7323 dated 15-6-1957 transferred the suit land in favour of Sub-Divisional Office, Chandpur. Later on, by gazette notification dated 14-3-195 Sub-Division has been upgraded as Pourashava and Hajigonj Pourashava was installed and defendant No. 1 became title holder of the suit property having possession thereto. In the suit land plaintiffs have no title hence the suit is liable to be dismissed with cost.

4. Both the courts below decreed the suit. In decreeing the suit both the courts below concurrently found that plaintiffs having able to prove their title from their predecessor and also proved they are continuously in possession over the suit land, they acquired title. Courts below considered the case of plaintiffs and after consultation of the papers was of the opinion that the aforesaid land is not land of Pourashava. Both the courts below in support of decision relied on a number of decisions.

5. Mr AQM Shafiullah, learned Advocate, appearing for the defendant No. 1 petitioner, canvass before us, only law point that as per section 152 of the Pourashava Ordinance, 1977 before filing of the suit, notice must be given to the Pourashava. Learned Advocate further submits that law as provided in the Ordinance is mandatory, absence of his suit cannot proceed. Mr AQM Shafiullah, learned Advocate relied of section 152 of the Pourashava Ordinance, 1977 and also on the case of Md Nurul Islam, Chairman, Kishurgonj Pourashava vs M/s Sheikh Enterprise, 21 BLD 565 = 6 BLC 47 and on the case of Noor Mohammad Khan and others vs Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and others, 42 DLR 434, on the case of Narayangonj Pourashava, represented by its Administrator, Narayangonj; Chairman, Narayangonj Paurashava vs Abdur Razzak 46 DLR 295. In all these decisions it is held that "before filing of any suit notice under section 152 of the Pourashava Ordinance 1977 must be served." Mr AQM Shafiullah, learned Advocate further submits that plaintiff did not produce any paper to show that plaintiffs' possession in the suit do not hit by provision of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and suit can proceed. Learned Advocate next relied on the case of Abul Bashar Sowdagar vs Bacha Meah, 11 MLR 354 = 59 DLR 112 wherein it is held as per section 91 of the Local Government Ordinance, 1976 and section 152 of the Paurashava Ordinance, 1977 were couched in identical language that provisions of service which prior of institution of suit against local Parishad is mandatory.

6. Mr Khair Ezaz Maswood, learned Advocate with Mrs Sakina Parveen with Mr Md Nazmul Huda, learned Advocates, appearing for the plaintiff-respondent-opposite parties, on the other hand, submits that, service of notice as per section 152 of the Pourashava Ordinance, 1977 is not mandatory but directory and relied on the case of Meharuddin (Md) vs Gouripur Pourashava, 2 BLC 88.

7. All these decisions referred by the parties goes to show that before institution of any suit, notice is required but question is whether service of notice is mandatory or directory. We find that the decision cited by petitioner is mandatory. Question for decision in this rule is very narrow i.e. construction of section 152 of the Pourashava Ordinance, 1977 which runs as follows—

"No suit shall be instituted against a Paurashava, or against any commissioner, officer or employee of a Paurashava in respect of any act done or purporting to be done in official capacity. until the expiration of one month next after notice in writing has been, in the case of Paurashava delivered or left at its office, and in the case of a commissioner, officer or employee, delivered to him or left at his office or place of abode, stating the cause of action and the name and place of abode of the intending plaintiff, and the plaint shall contain a statement that such notice has been so delivered or left."

<u>8. On consultation of the earlier decisions we are very sorry to mention that all these decisions goes to show that any kind of suit if filed then service of such notice is mandatory. But it is our considered view that all the decisions of both petitioner and opposite parties missed the line, as they missed to notice that this section is mandatory when any of the employee or commissioner or officer or any Paurashava does any act or purporting to any act in official capacity, that means, if any officer, employee or commissioner of Pourashava does any act in respect of duties cast upon them under Pourashava Ordinance, 1977 chapter-1 and 2 of the Pourashava then notice is mandatory. It may be explained in this way that if Pourashava want to construct a road or sewerage line which affect the land of any citizen, then if any legal proceeding be taken, in that case, notice is mandatory or if any employee, commissioner or officer direct in his official capacity to a citizen to do certain act then also in taking any legal proceeding, notice is mandatory, i.e. any citizen when aggrieved want to file a suit against such act of the employee or commissioner or officer of Pourashava in such cases notice are required. It will not be applicable for other purpose i.e. if anyone files any suit for title, as the case in hand, such notice need not be served upon Pourashava. Construction of this section has been wrongly applied in the decisions cited before us. Since law has been given a different meaning by the decisions cited, the decisions are not universally applicable but the decisions are per incuriam. Since only ground learned Advocate for the petitioner canvassed we find that courts below committed no illegality in decreeing the suit. We find no substance in the rule.</u>

9. In the result, the rule is discharged without any order as to costs.

10. Send down the lower court records.

Communicate this judgment at once.

End.
